notes.decision: Preserved as a section-marker symbol. Likely an ornamental phi or paragraphos delimiting the chapter heading.

Greek χαῖρε/χαρά. In context (paired with ⲉⲓⲣⲏⲛⲏ 'peace' and connected with ἀσπασμός 'salutation'), this is the formal greeting/salutation 'rejoice.' Translating 'greeting' to preserve the greeting-formula sense rather than abstract 'joy.'

Translated as 'an obeisance with which they pay obeisance to one another' — preserving the cognate construction (verb + cognate object) which the Coptic foregrounds. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ here is both the act and the salutation-gesture.

Read as ⲧⲁ-ⲛⲓⲙ ⲧⲉ 'whose is it?' — the disciples' question concerns whom the chirotonia belongs to / pertains to. Could also be 'of what kind' but the genitive interrogative is the more natural reading.

Read as a presentational 'behold' (≈ ⲉⲓⲥ) introducing the enumeration. Form is unusual; possibly a Lycopolitan presentational particle. Translated 'Behold these five kinds:' to fit the catalogue structure that follows.
ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ here = Sahidic ⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'kind, sort, manner' — distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' (different lexeme). Translated 'kinds' consistently throughout.
Read as Lycopolitan variant of ⲡⲥⲏⲩ 'the time' (parallel to ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲡ in lines 2, 21, 30). The orthography ⲥⲭⲩ for ⲥⲏⲩ is unusual but contextually demanded.

Translated tentatively as 'their hand' — possibly a Coptic adaptation of Greek χείρ (cf. χειροτονία in lines 1-4 of this very passage about laying-on of hands). The series 'peace / hand / blessing / joy' fits a sequence of greeting-gestures. Confidence low; could alternatively be a verb of obeisance.
Translated tentatively as 'their joy/triumph' — ⲃⲣⲟ possibly Lycopolitan reflex of a root for exultation/triumph. Fits the sequence of greeting-elements but lexical identification uncertain.
Doubled ⲧ likely scribal dittography or dialectal feature; treated as 'The first' parallel to lines 12, 19, 29.
Translated 'they were sending him forth' — ⲧϩⲡⲟ likely related to ⲑⲡⲟ 'cause to depart, escort.' The ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' confirms a verb of dispatching/sending out.

Lexical identification uncertain. Context ('coming forth to the X of the lower side') suggests a synonym for ⲁⲅⲱⲛ 'contest' or related word for combat/descent. Translated as '[combat]' tentatively in the apparatus.

Translated 'who belongs to the house of the men.' ⲏⲡ is the qualitative of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, number' — to be counted/reckoned as belonging. The 'house of the men' is the kingdom (cf. line 11), the heavenly home from which the First Man set out and to which he returns.

Translated tentatively 'the contest.' Lexeme not in standard lexica; context (parallel with ⲁⲣⲱⲛ 'battle' in line 6 and ⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ in line 10) requires a noun for combat or arena. Possibly a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲗⲍ̄ 'engage, struggle' nominalized, or a specialized cosmogonic term.

ⲡⲁⲣⲱⲛ rendered consistently 'the battle' on the basis of repeated parallelism with ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ (line 10 and 16). Likely a Lycopolitan or Manichaean technical noun for the cosmic war. ⲡⲉϩⲁⲣⲱⲛ in line 6 = ⲡⲉϥ-ⲁⲣⲱⲛ 'his battle.'

Translated 'the five signs.' ⲙⲉⲓ̈ⲉ likely Lycopolitan plural of ⲙⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'sign, token,' standing in synonymous parallel with ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ. Alternative readings: 'likenesses' or 'kinds' — but signs/tokens fit best with the ritual-typological context (each mystery = a heavenly act manifest in an earthly sign).
Translated 'he humbled him, he prevailed.' ⲑⲃⲓⲟ = humble, lay low; ⲃⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ = prevail over, conquer. The two verbs name the act of subduing the enemy.

Translated 'the summoning' (lit. 'the calling out, the call'). ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ = ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call, summon, invite.' Here treated as the agentive entity (the divine Call) which gave the peace. Cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'summon forth' — same root.

Translated 'to whom they were sent, whom they hearkened to, [as] a giving among the powers.' ⲧⲁⲩⲧⲉⲛ likely = ⲧⲁⲩⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲩ 'they sent (her),' contracted; ⲥⲁⲧⲙⲉⲥ = ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄+3fs 'they obeyed/hearkened to her.' ⲟⲩⲧⲱⲩ uncertain — possibly a verbal noun of ⲧ/ϯ 'give' (cf. line 23 ⲉⲩⲧ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ 'while they give it'), or a writing of ⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'between/among.' Tentative reading combines both possibilities.
Parsed as ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲉ-ϥ-ⲛ̄ⲧⲍ 'when he brought him up' — temporal converter + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('bring') + 3sg.m. object. The Living Spirit brought the First Man up out of the battle.

Translated 'as a custom.' Form not in standard lexica; rendering inferred from context (the divine kiss exists 'as X among the men, that they kiss one another'). Possibly = ⲟⲩⲱⲧϩ̄ 'a copying/repetition' or related to 'practice, repeated act.' Reading parallels ⲟⲩⲧⲱⲩ in line 19 — both likely name the earthly counterpart-mode of the heavenly mystery.

Parsed as ⲉⲩ- + ⲁⲧ- (privative) + ϩⲛⲁⲩ ('see/sight') = 'while they are without seeing.' Fits the contrast: people who travel apart and cannot see one another physically still embrace 'in the mystery of that kiss.' The earthly embrace bridges spatial separation precisely because it shares the heavenly mystery's substance.

Translated 'the second' here and in lines 20, 25 — though referring sequentially to the third, fourth, fifth mysteries. The Lycopolitan ⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ/ⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲧⲉ ('second' m./f.) appears used iteratively here, possibly with the sense 'the next/further [mystery]' or 'the second [instance, i.e. earthly form] of X.' The text emphasizes that each mystery has a heavenly act and a corresponding 'second' enacted form — divine + earthly correspondence pair.
Translated 'this gaze of God.' ⲛⲉⲩ = ⲛⲁⲩ 'see, look, gaze' nominalized. The First Man worships in/within the gaze of the God of Truth — i.e. under his face/presence.

Obscure verb in physically-present text. Context (Father of Life + Mother of Living + Man up from the Deep + 'toward the mystery') suggests a verb of motion/passage. Possibly Greek-derived παράγω 'pass through, pass forth' adapted to Lycopolitan; or related to ⲡⲱⲣⲱ 'extend.' Tentatively rendered 'had passed forth.' Not in apparatus because the text is physically present.
ⲛ̄ here read as the verb 'bring' (Sahidic ⲉⲓⲛⲉ in its conjugated form ⲛ̄-) with First Man as object. The Living Spirit 'brings' the First Man up from the war — standard Manichaean cosmogonic action.
= ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ 'wave.' The First Man is rescued from 'all the waves' of the war with Darkness — standard Manichaean cosmogonic image.
ⲍⲣⲁⲩ = ϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'voice' with 3pl suffix. 'Their voice came to him from on high' — the Lights of the upper realm address the ascending First Man with the words of Ps 110:1.
'My firstborn' — ϣⲁⲙⲓⲥⲉ = ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ per accumulated vocabulary. Here applied to the First Man as God's firstborn, addressed in the words of Ps 110:1.
Read as ϫⲉ-ⲉϥⲁ-ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'so that he might become' (purposive ϫⲉ + future). Fits the syntactical context of receiving ordination in order to become leader.
'The great gives authority to the small' (ⲧ = ϯ 'give'). The ecclesiastical correspondence to the First Man's enthronement: the rite of ordination as transmission of authority from greater to lesser.
= Sahidic ϭⲟⲙ 'power.' Lycopolitan ⲅ for ϭ. 'The powers of darkness' — standard Manichaean designation for the archonic forces in whose midst Mankind exists.

Read as ⲧⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'the Mind' (with apparent dittography or assimilation of ⲡ→ⲧ before ⲛ). The Light-Mind (νοῦς) is the technical Manichaean term for the descending intellectual savior. Confirmed by ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ in line 32.
The repetition 'type, type' = 'type by type' — the descending Mind manifests in successive correspondential figures, each replicating the same divine pattern. Standard Manichaean typological idiom.
Lycopolitan = ϣⲁϫⲉ 'word, saying.' 'The five words' likely refers to the fivefold ritual formula (peace, right hand, kiss, etc.) by which the Mind greets the Church.
'Greet, embrace' — semantic match with ⲡⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('kiss/embrace') in line 33. The Mind's 'greeting' is the cosmological prototype of the ecclesial kiss of peace.
Restored as form of ⲧⲱⲍ 'join, mix, attach' (Sahidic ⲧⲱϩ) + 3sg.m suffix + ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ 'into the Church.' The Mind's drawing-and-joining concludes the soteriological reception sequence.

Restored as ἀσπασμὸς τῆς ἀγάπης 'kiss of love (agape)' — the holy kiss attested in Pauline letters (Rom 16:16, etc.) and continued as Manichaean ecclesial practice. The line-34 surviving ⲡⲏ confirms the ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ ending.

Treated as a Lycopolitan habitual 3pl form ϣⲁϩ-ⲩ-(ⲗ-)ⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ̄ ('they habitually worship'), with the ϩⲭ cluster reflecting an unusual orthography for ϣⲁⲩ-. The intervening ⲗ may be a verbal prefix or a scribal peculiarity. The semantic content (ⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ̄ 'worship,' echoed by following ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲩⲱϣⲧ̄) is clear.

ⲧⲍⲁⲏ = Sah. ⲧϩⲁⲏ 'the end, the last.' Translated 'the last of these' (i.e., the fifth and culminating gesture in the sacramental sequence). The five gestures match the enumeration in lines 28–29: peace, right hand, kiss, worship, cheirotonia.

Reading as ⲛⲥ̄-ⲥⲁⲣ-ⲟⲩ 'and she ⲥⲁⲣs them,' where ⲥⲁⲣ = Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱⲣ/ⲥⲱⲗ 'remove, draw away.' Soteriological context (Form of Light leading the soul out of darkness toward light) supports 'draws them away.'

Both from root ϩⲣⲁϫ/ϩⲣⲟⲕ 'be calm, still, at peace.' ⲧⲍⲣⲕⲟ = causative 'she stills, calms'; ⲡⲉⲥⲍⲣⲁⲕ = noun 'her stillness, her calm.' The Form of Light stills the dying elect with her kiss and her stillness — a peace-giving counterpart to the demons' ⲍⲣⲧⲉ ('fear').
Continuing the ϩⲣⲁⲕ-root semantics: 'the heart of the elect... is at peace concerning him/in him.' Same lexical field as ⲡⲉⲥⲍⲣⲁⲕ in segment 13.

Tentatively rendered 'embrace,' interpreting as Greek ἀγάπη (love-feast/embrace) with anomalous ⲗⲁ for ⲅⲁ. The pairing ⲡⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ + ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ (kiss + love) is a standard liturgical doublet. Confidence low; flagged as proposed term.

Parsed as ⲧⲉⲥ- ('her') + ⲣⲁϩ- (= ⲣⲉϥ- 'one who') + ⲥⲱⲧⲉ ('redeem'): 'her redeemer.' Identified in line 21 as 'the form of light' — i.e., the soul's heavenly counterpart/Twin who descends at the moment of death.
Unidentified noun. Possible readings: 'fathers' (Lyc ⲁⲓⲱⲧⲉ) with possessive ⲛϩ-, or 'garments/treasures.' Left untranslated/transliterated as 'hayeute' pending parallels. Flagged as proposed term.
Tentatively analyzed as jussive ⲙⲁⲣⲉ- + verbal element ⲕⲱⲛ̄ ('remain, be set'). Translated 'let... remain.' The full sense: 'let these five signs remain in your hands honored before each of you.'

Translated as 'bishops.' The word stands in the standard Manichaean ecclesiastical hierarchy between teachers (ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ = didaskaloi) and presbyters, the slot occupied by ἐπίσκοποι (the 72 bishops). The Coptic etymology is unclear to me — possibly a native Coptic plural from a root for 'oversee/examine' (cf. ϣⲱⲙⲧ̄), but I cannot verify. Rendered by ecclesiastical-position rather than by etymology, with this caveat.

Reading ⲁⲓ̈- as 1sg perfect: 'those whom I ordained.' The following clause ⲁⲓ̈ⲕⲱ ⲁⲭⲱⲩ 'I have set upon them' confirms 1sg subject continuity. Mani himself is the speaker who ordained the church orders.
Translated 'shall turn aside.' ⲧⲥⲧⲁⲥ here = ⲧⲥⲧⲟ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'turn back/aside, apostatize.' Coptic causative ⲧⲥⲧⲟ from ⲥⲧⲟ 'turn,' with the spatial particle ⲁⲃⲁⲗ preserving the away-direction.
Translated 'gather yourselves in.' ⲱⲱⲧⲡ may be a Lyc. reduplicated form of ⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'shut, join, embrace,' here reflexive imperative with ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'into.' Functions as 'assemble/bind yourselves into.'

Tentatively rendered 'the persuasion.' Possibly ⲁ-ⲧ-ⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ where ⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ = Greek πειθώ 'persuasion' or πίστις 'trust' through dialectal phonology. The exhortation 'gather yourselves into the persuasion of [you/your...]' fits a closing paraenetic context. Proposing as new term pending parallels.
Parsed as ⲩ̈- (3pl future) + ⲛⲁⲩ ('see') + ϩⲩ̈ (= ϩⲱⲟⲩ 'themselves'): 'they themselves shall see (you).' The reflexive intensifier is well-attested in Lyc.
Translated 'suppliants.' Greek-derived noun, likely αἰτητής 'asker, claimant' (or pl. αἰτηταί). Article ⲛ- before, preserving the petitionary semantics of asking before God.
